rule: Historical repair durations are analogues, not automatic copies. Branch damage type, transit, emergency repair, yard capacity, parts and air-group regeneration are separate clocks.

USS_Independence_CVL22.confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH; shifted analogue of historical one-torpedo damage

USS_Lexington_CV16.damage: 1 aerial torpedo + 1-2 bomb hits; machinery/steering plus flight-deck/hangar damage; survives at ~18-22 kt after stabilization
USS_Lexington_CV16.emergency: Pearl Harbor arrival center 1943-12-02..04; 1-2 weeks emergency/temporary work
USS_Lexington_CV16.confidence: MEDIUM; branch estimate deliberately longer than historical 12/4 torpedo-only repair

USS_Yorktown_CV10.damage: 1 bomb + near-miss damage, temporary flight-deck interruption
USS_Yorktown_CV10.yard_note: Short December Pearl availability if operational tempo permits; no strategic long-term absence

IJN_Soryu.damage: 2 bomb hits flight deck/hangar; local hangar fire; propulsion/waterline not critically damaged

IJN_Fujinami.damage: light-moderate 5-inch/splinter damage during stand-off raid withdrawal; machinery remains usable

USS_Pierce_APA50.damage: 1 submarine torpedo, aft/engine or hold damage; survives
USS_Pierce_APA50.major_repair: US west-coast or Pearl yard depending survey

I175.damage: heavy depth-charge shock/leaks after Pierce attack, but propulsion/diving control retained enough to escape

Japan.note: Includes first-line survivors plus secondary-carrier/rear pools; not all can be massed in one strike. Soryu survivors are cross-decked or ferried to Junyo/Hiyo/Ryujo/Zuiho and shore training/reconstitution nodes. The binding debt is experienced strike leadership/navigation/torpedo crew, not raw airframe count.

United_States.note: Independence/Lexington orphan aircraft are cross-decked or ferried to land bases/surviving decks. Material regeneration is faster than Japan; trained carrier-group integration and deck-space congestion still create short-term friction.
